notes:
PASS on the fake backend, final gate run. Served device mhs://localhost/kbot-flat, kind world.sim, mode simulated, risk R0 (the card's floor and the floors of cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1). The model is the card's models[0], playground/kbot/xmls/scene_mjx_feetonly_flat_terrain.xml, read in place from the pinned clone robots/kscalelabs/mujoco_playground (never copied, imported, installed or modified). It includes playground/kbot/xmls/kbot.xml: one free joint and 20 hinges (27 qpos, 26 dof) and 20 position actuators. The robot default class's inheritrange 1 makes each actuator ctrlrange equal the matching joint range, so the bridge derives action.ctrl's 20 per-actuator bounds from the model and the package writes no Limit of its own. kbot.xml declares no <option timestep>, so the MuJoCo engine default 0.002 s applies; the bridge reads the step from the loaded model. The fake backend is fake.py, a callable stand-in mujoco module that parses the same scene and include for the step, the coordinates and the ctrlranges and integrates a placeholder first-order motion. Because a callable fake is treated as the upstream simulator, the gate warns G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND (there is no package fake class surface to record), and G8.NO_UNIT x3 for the family-derived inputs ticks, action.ctrl[*] and the reset seed; these are the expected simulator-family warnings. G4 had no REF_VALUE or REF_BINARY warnings. NOT COVERED: the MuJoCo engine was not installed and was never run; the fake computes no inertias, contacts, friction, meshes or actuator or sensor dynamics, so its trajectories are not MuJoCo results; cap.world.reset.v1 calls mj_resetData and starts from the model defaults (the free body at its XML pose z 1.08006263 with an identity quaternion and zero hinge angles), not from a keyframe, and the scene's keyframe block is commented out; no rendering, cameras or sensor streams are served; the sim backend (the real mujoco module loading the same scene) was not run; snapshot and restore are advertised and the stand-in implements the bridge's integration-state calls, but the gate does not exercise them; the mesh and texture assets are not loaded by the stand-in; the model is a simulation asset and no physical K-Bot is modelled or controlled, and no hardware run is claimed. The package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null); a simulator has no hardware backend at all, so no hardware protection is claimed. Only catalogue classes are used, so there are no catalogue requests. gate.digest is the digest the check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
